The arithmetic against the two sides of the merge, which is where the number comes from rather than from a sweep that was never re-run: this branch carried 516 (492 at its base, plus its own 18 `chat-run-details` frames) and main carried 506 - the same set with this branch's 18 frames replaced by #106's 8 new `chat-tool-rows` frames - and a merge keeps both sides' frames, so 516 + 8 = 524. `check-evidence.mjs` is what confirms it; the figures are recorded here because a reader who cannot re-derive them has no way to tell a reconciled manifest from one that was edited until the gate passed.

USAGE REVIEW ROUND 1: all twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the round changed what they show, not merely how they look. Two of them were the point: `loading` and `fetching` previously photographed states the shipped container could not produce (an ENABLED `Ask providers now` at first paint, when react-query reports isLoading and isFetching together; and cached numbers retained during a live ask, which the query key switch discarded). USAGE REVIEW ROUND 2 (remediation): the same twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the scroll-fold treatment changed what most of them show. The fold rule is no longer an unconditional per-picker prop: it is measured per state from the scroll container, so the six states whose content ends above the fold (`empty`, `query-error`, `fetching`, `percent-only`, `remaining-balance`, `narrow`) no longer draw a boundary under nothing, and the states that do overflow carry a `border-control` rule (3:1 structural floor, pinned at the call site in scripts/contrast-contract.mjs) plus a 20px bottom fade that retracts at the end of the list. `loading` also changed copy: the first paint reads `Reading cached usage` rather than `Asking providers`, because opening the view is a cache read and not a provider ask. No story was added or deleted, so `frames` (498) and `surfaces` (57) are unchanged and still equal what is on disk. `real-data/` was NOT re-captured this round and is STALE with respect to the fold treatment: it still shows the round-1 clip. The fold fix was instead verified at that exact density in the interaction harness - 11 provider blocks, 22 windows, 1217px of content in a 520px box - measuring a 1px `border-control` rule and a gradient mask at the top of the scroll and the mask retracted with the rule still present at the bottom, in both brand themes. Everything else `real-data` is evidence for (the staleness baseline, the description line, the multi-account keying) is unaffected by this round's changes. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 3: the story `chat-usage--dense` was ADDED (the thirteenth chat-usage surface, 2 frames in the two brand themes), so `frames` (498 -> 500) and `surfaces` (57 -> 58) were corrected by hand per the accounting rule above. It exists because the only committed frame at overflowing density was `real-data/`, which is one commit stale against the fold treatment and cannot be re-derived on demand; `dense` is the same density built from fixtures - eleven reports, twenty-eight windows, five anthropic accounts, the identities and labels the real response shapes - so any sweep can re-take it. The fold it photographs was measured in the same session against the same Storybook build, in both brand themes: 1273px of content in the 520px body cap (753px hidden), a 20px gradient mask plus a 1px `border-control` rule on the wrapper at scrollTop 0, the mask RETRACTED with the rule still present at scrollTop max, and no treatment at all on a fitting state (`percent-only` measured 0px hidden, no mask, 0px border). `real-data/` was NOT re-captured, and this time the live refill was attempted for real: the exact request the button makes (GET /v1/desktop/usage?live=true&refresh=true, authenticated with the running server's own desktop bearer) answered source=live with ZERO reports in ~50ms, and explicit per-provider asks for every usage-capable provider also returned zero - the backend's current credential view has no usage-reportable providers, so its cache cannot be refilled from here. `real-data/` therefore remains stale with respect to the fold treatment, its staleness stays recorded, and the fold at real density is evidenced by `dense`, which is re-derivable. REBASE ONTO main, THREE HOPS: this branch was cut from 2217ea59a and rebased first onto #114's head (104b0321a, the write/edit diff body), then onto 1f241ba87 (#111's backend-composed toasts plus the 0.17.1 release bump), and finally onto 4455c5705 (#107's update-installer safety work plus the 0.17.2 release bump) - each time because main moved while the gates were running. The thirteen `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED at this head (26 frames, both brand themes) because `capture-evidence.mjs` itself changed in the merge and #107 changed `src/main` and `src/preload`, so `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` above name the commit these frames actually came from and it is reachable on this branch. All 26 reproduced BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the pre-rebase set the review, QA, design and UX rounds signed off - same SHA-256 for every file - which is the measured evidence that none of #114, #111 or #107 changed anything this view renders and that the design sign-off still describes the pixels on the current head. The capture ran with `--allow-backend` because a backend belonging to another session was listening on the configured port; that flag is sound here and only here because every `chat-usage` story renders `UsageDialog`, which by construction does no fetching (the query lives in `UsageView`, which no story renders), and the byte-identical result is itself the proof that no live reply reached a frame. The two `chat-usage/real-data` frames were NOT re-captured and are the same bytes as before, so their recorded staleness against the round-2 fold treatment is unchanged and still accurate - a rebase does not make a frame fresher. #107's, #114's and the older `tui-parity/` frames are byte-identical to main: the `--only=chat-usage` runs wrote nothing outside `chat-usage/`. So the frames in this tree come from four heads, not one: `chat-usage/` story frames from this head 69664578f, `common-updatenotification/` and `update-robustness/` from #107's own capture, `write-edit-diff/` from #114's own capture at 96171dac, and the older sweep frames from the August head as recorded above.

THIS BRANCH (fix/tool-row-args-recovery) ON TOP OF THAT: the tool row's object column is recovered from a mid-turn snapshot's seed, which carries settling frames and no arguments — so rows that read `exit code: 0`, `Edited <path>`, `result: None` or a bare line number now name the call. REMEDIATION ROUND: the eighteen `chat-run-details` frames were re-taken at `48d1357ab` (Storybook on 6017, `--only=run-details --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight --allow-backend`), the first capture this branch has taken since it was merged with `origin/main`: `dirtyWorkingTree` is false and the two tree hashes name that commit. All eighteen moved, where the previous round had thirteen byte-identical - the story now paints `canvas` under the popover instead of `surface` (#113), so a ground pixel that read `(30,26,21)` dark reads `(23,19,14)` now. At zero fuzz that is 29-85% of each frame's pixels, which is a 7-unit channel step and not damage; the two causes are separable at stated thresholds, because an 8% fuzz is a 20-unit channel tolerance and larger than that step. At 8% the only frames with any differing pixel at all are the ones whose CONTENT changed - `crowded` (870 dark / 838 light) and `subagents-only` (3801 / 3979), whose rows the slice now selects by the children's own clocks, plus `both-in-flight` light (83) for its live clock. The panel's own separation was re-measured on the new ground: dark L* 6.14 -> 13.62 and light 95.28 -> 99.43, against the 4.41 / 1.78 step the previous set certified over `surface`. Two of the fixtures changed shape with the code: `crowded` is now stored deliberately out of chronological order, so the frame is a guard for the tie-break rather than a picture that agrees with every rule, and it no longer carries a `paused` row - a state this wire cannot produce. `frames` (516) and `surfaces` (75) are unchanged by the round: no frame was added or removed.
